rounds.reviewer: repo owner (szablevi@gmail.com), in-session review with the coding agent
rounds.purpose: Second manual spot-check of a random sample of translated artefacts against their original source material, human evidence supplementing the automated QA suite (issue #103), run against the domain's current state after the disposition-judging fix and reinstate.py additions. Supersedes the first spot-check round (2026-08-17, pre-rerun) whose sampled artefact population no longer exists after the full clean pipeline rerun.
rounds.artefact_definition: Every individually source-mapped element in translation.json's `mappings` list: classes, class properties, relationships, rules, actions (127 total at sampling time). Competency questions excluded (synthesized from the whole domain, not mapped from specific source IRIs).

sampling_method.description: Stratified sample by artefact type, proportional allocation with round-to-nearest, fixed random seed for reproducibility.

notes: One real defect found and fixed during this round: relationships[31] (Thermostat serves Zone) had genuinely strong evidence -- a verbatim quote from Zone's real source definition, plus an unclaimed matching real relation (rec#servicedBy) -- but source_iris was empty, making the mapping unverifiable by anything except a human reading the prose. Root cause was general (repair.py's reground action never asked for source_iris as structured data), fixed in repair.py itself (not just this one mapping) with tests, then reapplied to this item and independently re-verified (unanimous supported).

One agent self-correction during this round: the agent initially misflagged actions.maintainWithinDeadband's rationale as a 'stale' leftover from before the clean rerun, referencing the action's pre-rename name (maintainCurrentMode). Challenged by the reviewer ('how can stale things be in there' given the full rerun claim). Investigated by diffing against the pre-repair compile output: the current rationale text is genuinely different from the original, proving it was freshly written during the repair-driven rename, not left untouched. The old name is referenced to explain the rename decision, which is legitimate, not a bug. Flag withdrawn.

items.reviewer_comment: Flagged: rationale says thermostat's setpoint-maintenance definition 'implies' sensor input, rather than stating it directly.

mapping.source_evidence: Zone is defined as a "space or group of spaces ... for which the heating, cooling, or lighting requirements are sufficiently similar that desired conditions can be maintained throughout by a single controlling device," and a Thermostat is "an automatic control device used to maintain temperature at a fixed or adjustable setpoint"; this supports a thermostat serving the zone it controls.
mapping.rationale: The existing Thermostat→Zone serves relationship is directly grounded by Zone's single-controlling-device definition together with Thermostat being a control device, and the cited servicedBy relation matches this semantics.

result.name: serves
result.meaning: A thermostat serves as a controlling device for a zone.

items.reviewer_comment: Flagged: source_iris was empty despite evidence text quoting Zone's real definition -- investigated further per reviewer request.
items.finding: REAL FINDING, FIXED: independently verified the quoted evidence ("maintained throughout by a single controlling device") is a genuine verbatim substring of Zone's real source definition, and found an additional real match (rec#servicedBy, an object property directly matching the 'serves' relationship concept) that also wasn't cited. Root cause: repair.py's reground action asked the LLM for source_evidence/confidence/rationale as free text, but never asked for source_iris as structured data -- so even an accurate, well-written evidence quote left the mapping unverifiable by anything except a human reading the prose. Fixed generally in repair.py (source_iris now required and validated on every reground/replace, not just this one item), and re-ran the reground call for this item with the fix: source_iris now correctly lists brick#Zone, brick#Thermostat, and rec#servicedBy. Independently re-judged after the fix: unanimous supported.

items.reviewer_comment: REAL FINDING, LED TO A FULL 127-MAPPING AUDIT: cited evidence was borrowed from an unrelated third class (Site) that documents Brick's general hasPart/isPartOf convention, rather than from Building or Floor's own definitions -- neither endpoint's real definition was cited at all. This one flag, once investigated, revealed the same 'names a real class without citing it' pattern across 42 of 127 mappings (33%). Root cause fixed in compiler-prompt.md (an explicit 'empty source_iris is fine, describe in prose instead' instruction was directly licensing it); all 42 existing mappings reground with real, verified source_iris.
